messages.author: c5cfd1d5ae8f5054
messages.subject: RevolutionR compile flags for MKL on Linux CentOs
parts:
I'm trying to use an intel phi card to gain threads for some code that uses foreach package. From the documentation, if RevoultionR Open is compiled with the -mic flag I can load it and call it from a master on the host. Where can I find out which compile flags were used to build RevolutionR MKL version.

I'm running CentOs 7.

messages.author: c5cfd1d5ae8f5054
messages.subject: Re: RevolutionR compile flags for MKL on Linux CentOs
parts:
Found a book on intel phi by Colfax International, where they detail the ssh route to parallel. If I compile a "node" version of R usinh -mmic flag and load it on the phi, I can use makePsockCluster on each of the nodes to use foreach to get parallel nodes running.

I'd been trying avoid procuring the intel compiler and building R, but it looks like it's necessary.

messages.author: b92b0e53baf64e49
messages.subject: Re: RevolutionR compile flags for MKL on Linux CentOs
parts:
Hello Terry,

Our compile flags can be found in ./configure line in the R.spec file.  In that line, we can see that we are not currently compiling with –mic flag.
 
However, you should be able to:
  1. Download the entire RRO source tree from https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO.
  2. Modify the ./configure line in the R.spec file.
  3. Rebuild RRO using the build instructions in the README.md file.
Please report back if you are successful in building from source with those instructions, or if you run into any issues when compiling.

— Josée
